title: Semaglutide vs Tirzepatide
summary: Two randomized trials compare them directly: SURMOUNT-5 in obesity without diabetes (72 weeks) and SURPASS-2 in type 2 diabetes (40 weeks). Both are approved medicines with EU labels on record; this page restates each trial result in plain English with its citation.

seo.title: Semaglutide vs Tirzepatide: Head-to-Head Trial Results
seo.description: Semaglutide vs tirzepatide from the head-to-head trials: weight loss, HbA1c, side effects, doses, who should avoid each and storage, every figure cited.

head_to_head.value: Randomized controlled trial, humans, n=751, 2025: The least-squares mean percent change in weight at week 72 was -20.2% (95% confidence interval [CI], -21.4 to -19.1) with tirzepatide and -13.7% (95% CI, -14.9 to -12.6) with semaglutide (P<0.001).
head_to_head.source_excerpt: The least-squares mean percent change in weight at week 72 was -20.2% (95% confidence interval [CI], -21.4 to -19.1) with tirzepatide and -13.7% (95% CI, -14.9 to -12.6) with semaglutide (P<0.001).
head_to_head.plain: In SURMOUNT-5, the head-to-head phase 3b trial in 751 adults with obesity but without type 2 diabetes, average weight loss at 72 weeks was 20.2% with tirzepatide and 13.7% with semaglutide, each at the highest dose people tolerated.

head_to_head.value: Randomized controlled trial, humans, n=751, 2025: The most common adverse events in both treatment groups were gastrointestinal, and most were mild to moderate in severity and occurred primarily during dose escalation.
head_to_head.source_excerpt: The most common adverse events in both treatment groups were gastrointestinal, and most were mild to moderate in severity and occurred primarily during dose escalation.
head_to_head.plain: In SURMOUNT-5 the most common side effects with both drugs were digestive; most were mild to moderate and occurred mainly while the dose was being raised.

head_to_head.value: Randomized controlled trial, humans, n=1879, 2021: Tirzepatide at all doses was noninferior and superior to semaglutide. Reductions in body weight were greater with tirzepatide than with semaglutide (least-squares mean estimated treatment difference, -1.9 kg, -3.6 kg, and -5.5 kg, respectively; P<0.001 for all comparisons).
head_to_head.source_excerpt: Tirzepatide at all doses was noninferior and superior to semaglutide. Reductions in body weight were greater with tirzepatide than with semaglutide (least-squares mean estimated treatment difference, -1.9 kg, -3.6 kg, and -5.5 kg, respectively; P<0.001 for all comparisons).
head_to_head.plain: In SURPASS-2, a 40-week trial in 1,879 people with type 2 diabetes, tirzepatide at 5, 10 and 15 mg lowered HbA1c more than semaglutide 1 mg, and weight fell by 1.9, 3.6 and 5.5 kg more than with semaglutide.

head_to_head.value: Randomized controlled trial, humans, n=1879, 2021: Serious adverse events were reported in 5 to 7% of the patients who received tirzepatide and in 3% of those who received semaglutide.
head_to_head.source_excerpt: Serious adverse events were reported in 5 to 7% of the patients who received tirzepatide and in 3% of those who received semaglutide.
head_to_head.plain: In SURPASS-2, serious adverse events were reported in 5 to 7% of people on tirzepatide and 3% on semaglutide.

head_to_head.value: Randomized controlled trial, humans, n=1879, 2021: The most common adverse events were gastrointestinal and were primarily mild to moderate in severity in the tirzepatide and semaglutide groups (nausea, 17 to 22% and 18%; diarrhea, 13 to 16% and 12%; and vomiting, 6 to 10% and 8%, respectively).
head_to_head.source_excerpt: The most common adverse events were gastrointestinal and were primarily mild to moderate in severity in the tirzepatide and semaglutide groups (nausea, 17 to 22% and 18%; diarrhea, 13 to 16% and 12%; and vomiting, 6 to 10% and 8%, respectively).
head_to_head.plain: In SURPASS-2, nausea affected 17 to 22% of people on tirzepatide and 18% on semaglutide, diarrhoea 13 to 16% and 12%, and vomiting 6 to 10% and 8%; most cases were mild to moderate.

head_to_head.value: Phase 3 clinical trial, humans, 2026: This study evaluated the cost-effectiveness (from the United States [US] societal perspective) of tirzepatide at its maximum-tolerated-dose (MTD) compared to semaglutide (MTD), both administered adjunct to a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity.
head_to_head.source_excerpt: This study evaluated the cost-effectiveness (from the United States [US] societal perspective) of tirzepatide at its maximum-tolerated-dose (MTD) compared to semaglutide (MTD), both administered adjunct to a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity.
head_to_head.plain: A 2026 cost study based on the phase 3 SURMOUNT-5 trial compared the US cost-effectiveness of tirzepatide and semaglutide at their highest tolerated doses, each with diet and exercise; the excerpt states the aim, not the result.

head_to_head.value: Human study, humans, n=376, 2026: Among 553 073 adults with at least one semaglutide ( n = 376 697) or tirzepatide ( n = 176 376) prescription and baseline weight availability, documented initiation within ±3 months of the first structured prescription was identified in 141 189 semaglutide patients and 62 040 tirzepatide patients.
head_to_head.source_excerpt: Among 553 073 adults with at least one semaglutide ( n = 376 697) or tirzepatide ( n = 176 376) prescription and baseline weight availability, documented initiation within ±3 months of the first structured prescription was identified in 141 189 semaglutide patients and 62 040 tirzepatide patients.
head_to_head.plain: In a 2026 records study of 553 073 adults prescribed semaglutide (376 697) or tirzepatide (176 376), starting the drug was documented for 141 189 semaglutide and 62 040 tirzepatide patients. It compares record-keeping, not drug effects.

head_to_head.value: Clinical trial, humans, 2026: Patients treated with tirzepatide lost more weight than those treated with semaglutide (mean reduction, 14.7 vs. 10.8%; P P < 0.001), accompanied by faster monthly weight-loss velocity (2.54 vs. 2.18%).
head_to_head.source_excerpt: Patients treated with tirzepatide lost more weight than those treated with semaglutide (mean reduction, 14.7 vs. 10.8%; P P < 0.001), accompanied by faster monthly weight-loss velocity (2.54 vs. 2.18%).
head_to_head.plain: A 2026 study reported that people on tirzepatide lost more weight than those on semaglutide (average 14.7% versus 10.8%), with faster monthly weight loss (2.54% versus 2.18%).

head_to_head.value: Human study, humans, n=920, 2026: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists demonstrate cardiovascular benefits; however, head-to-head comparisons between semaglutide and tirzepatide remain limited.
head_to_head.source_excerpt: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists demonstrate cardiovascular benefits; however, head-to-head comparisons between semaglutide and tirzepatide remain limited.
head_to_head.plain: Background: a 2026 study using records to mimic a trial notes that GLP-1 drugs have heart benefits but direct semaglutide-versus-tirzepatide comparisons remain limited; the excerpt gives no result.

head_to_head.value: Animal study, mice, 2026: Given the therapeutic potential of GLP-1 receptor agonists (semaglutide, tirzepatide, and retatrutide) in diabetic nephropathy, we evaluated their anti-fibrotic and anti-inflammatory effects in non-diabetic renal fibrosis using HK-2 cells and murine UUO and aging models.
head_to_head.source_excerpt: Given the therapeutic potential of GLP-1 receptor agonists (semaglutide, tirzepatide, and retatrutide) in diabetic nephropathy, we evaluated their anti-fibrotic and anti-inflammatory effects in non-diabetic renal fibrosis using HK-2 cells and murine UUO and aging models.
head_to_head.plain: In a 2026 study using mice and kidney cells grown in a lab, researchers compared semaglutide, tirzepatide and retatrutide on kidney scarring and inflammation; the excerpt states the aim, not which did better.

5 research statements rewritten in plain english, each followed by a numbered citation mark linking to its source. The pages no longer show sentences copied from abstracts; those stay on file for the reviewer. Statements that turned out to say nothing about this compound are hidden pending review.
